description: A Mathematics major with a strong theoretical foundation who is transitioning to Computer Science and feels more comfortable with abstract logic than low-level implementation.

nodes.personalizationRationale: For a student with no prior exposure to C++, we begin by mapping their existing procedural logic to C++ fundamental syntax.
nodes.title: C++ Fundamentals for Python/Java Programmers
nodes.description: An introduction to C++ syntax and the compilation process, focusing on bridging knowledge from other languages.

nodes.title: Understanding Pointers & Memory Addresses
nodes.description: A deep dive into address-of operators, dereferencing, and the concept of the stack vs heap.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This student's no_prior_exposure status necessitates a dedicated deep-dive into C++ pointers to prevent confusion in later data structure implementations.

nodes.description: Exploring how C++ handles memory through references and how it differs from pointer-based access.
nodes.title: References and Parameter Passing
nodes.personalizationRationale: Because the student has no prior exposure to C++, we must explicitly clarify pass-by-reference mechanics before moving to complex object-oriented design.

nodes.description: Designing robust C++ classes with constructors, destructors, and member functions.
nodes.title: Classes and Object-Oriented Design
nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard curriculum coverage of C++ class design is necessary for this student to meet the final exam proficiency requirements.

nodes.title: Generic Programming & Exception Handling
nodes.description: Implementing reusable code using C++ templates and managing runtime errors with exceptions.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Every student must master templates and exceptions as they are central to the course's subsequent implementation of generic data structures.
This core module ensures the student masters the first fundamental data structure and its associated performance metrics.
nodes.description: Implementation of singly, doubly, and circularly linked lists with Big-O analysis of their operations.
nodes.title: Arrays and Linked List Architectures

nodes.description: Assessment covering recursive algorithm design and basic asymptotic notation.
nodes.title: Quiz 1: Recursion & Asymptotics
nodes.personalizationRationale: This required assessment verifies the student's grasp of recursion before moving on to more complex sequence-based structures.
Mastering the LIFO and FIFO properties of stacks and queues is a non-negotiable requirement for the cumulative midterm exam.
nodes.description: Implementing Stacks and Queues using both arrays and linked lists.
nodes.title: Stacks, Queues, and Deques

nodes.personalizationRationale: Understanding vector resizing and iterator invalidation is a standard requirement for all students in this cumulative course.
nodes.description: Deep dive into the Vector ADT and the mechanics of STL-style iterators.
nodes.title: Vectors and Iterator Mechanics

nodes.description: Analyzing sequence ADTs and the implementation of Bubble Sort.
nodes.title: Sequence ADTs & Bubble Sort Analysis
nodes.personalizationRationale: Sequential data structures and basic sorting analysis form the basis for the more advanced algorithms taught later in the course.

nodes.description: Comprehensive review and assessment of all material from C++ foundations through sequence structures.
nodes.title: Midterm Review & Assessment Checkpoint
nodes.personalizationRationale: As required by the course structure, this assessment ensures the student is prepared for the high-stakes midterm examination.
This node introduces the foundational non-linear data structures required for the latter half of the semester.
nodes.title: General Trees and Traversals
nodes.description: General tree definitions, properties, and traversal strategies (depth-first and breadth-first).

nodes.title: Binary Tree Structures
nodes.description: Properties of binary trees and their array-based vs linked implementations.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Binary trees are a core exam topic, necessitating a detailed study of their mathematical properties and implementation details.
Even as a smaller block, the heap data structure is mandatory due to its role in efficient sorting and scheduling algorithms.
nodes.title: Priority Queues & Heaps
nodes.description: Implementing priority queues using binary heaps and analyzing 'up-heap' and 'down-heap' operations.

nodes.title: Maps and Hash Tables
nodes.description: Designing hash functions and handling collisions using chaining and open addressing.
nodes.personalizationRationale: The student must understand the trade-offs in hash table design as part of the core data structure proficiency requirements.
This foundational search tree module is required to prepare the student for more complex balanced tree proofs.
nodes.description: Implementation and analysis of Binary Search Trees and the AVL balancing property.
nodes.title: BST and AVL Trees

nodes.personalizationRationale: Advanced tree structures are heavily tested in the final blocks, requiring focused core study on their balancing logic.
nodes.title: Multi-Way & Red-Black Trees
nodes.description: Structural analysis of Red-Black trees and (2,4) trees for maintaining logarithmic search time.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Efficiency analysis of different sorting paradigms is a central learning objective that every student must demonstrate.
nodes.title: Merge Sort and Selection Sort Efficiency
nodes.description: Comparative analysis of Selection Sort and Merge Sort, including divide-and-conquer strategy.
Synthesizing the semester's material through a course capstone review of data structure selection.
nodes.title: Data Structure Selection & Capstone Review
nodes.personalizationRationale: The capstone review prepares the student to apply their cumulative knowledge to complex problem-solving scenarios on the final exam.
This required final checkpoint ensures the student has integrated all course concepts, satisfying the cumulative assessment requirement.
nodes.description: Final cumulative assessment and comprehensive review covering all course objectives from Block 01 to Block 08.
nodes.title: Quiz 4 & Cumulative Final Review
